admission.justification: The obligation is split between the pure decision that recognises a call, tests the hand-off, scopes the turn's rows and chooses between the seat's message and the parent's marked line, and the host handler that reads the host's agent state and writes the plugin's own log; the host-free suite proves the recognised row shapes, the silence and send gates, the count and its reset, and the log rows.

applicability: Every `agent.turn_ended` event the AR Paseo plugin handles for a role agent the product's agent list holds, and every role launch whose agent the plugin's own provider verdict puts on an ACP connection.
conditions: The plugin recognises a call in every row shape it may arrive in: the bare name, `<server>.<tool>`, and each Hermes title with or without a preview; a row whose ACP kind is not an AR kind is never an AR call.
The answer is read from Codex's `output` or from Hermes's text in either wrapper after one unescape, and a cut answer is read as far as it shows.
The recipient is read from Codex's `input` or from a Hermes answer that names it; a row that shows no recipient is a hand-off where it is one but never a return to the parent.

A turn hands off on a `role_message` whose finished answer is not `refused`, `ok: false` or `recipient-busy`, or on a `task_doc` write that is not `ok: false`; a leaf seat starts no role, so `role_start` is not its hand-off.

The turn's rows are those after the seat's previous end as this build saw it — its remembered row count and last row identity — falling back to the last `user_message` on the first end seen or when a replaced timeline no longer holds that row.

An end is silent only when the turn completed, holds no hand-off, does not end with an `IDENTITY MISMATCH:` line, declares no helper or background wait, and the seat is open and unarchived, owes no permission and has no child agent in a turn, and the end is not a reply to a waiting sender in a turn; a child is an agent whose `paseo.parent-agent-id` label names the seat, and only an exhausted host listing supplies these facts.

Every silent end waits 60 seconds before it acts, the counted parent line included; a turn of the seat that starts inside the wait cancels the send and the end is not counted, and at the end of the wait a seat that is closed, in a turn, archived or owing a permission is left alone, with the skip written and the end not counted.

The first two silent ends in a row send the seat a message with the plugin's own fixed first line, naming its role and task, quoting the ended turn's last line, saying the turn ended with no hand-off, and asking it to go on with its stage or to send what blocks it to its parent; a turn whose rows hold a `delegate_task` call adds that a helper's result does not come back as a message, and the closing instruction names the declaration: on an ACP seat one sentence that names it among the ways to end a turn and asks for a progress report naming each helper, what it does, its status and what came back, on any other seat the helper-declaration sentence, and on every seat the sentence that names the background declaration.

From the third silent end in a row the seat receives nothing and its parent receives the line marked with the count; the count is per seat agent id and returns to zero on a hand-off or on a turn begun by a message the plugin did not send.
Only Worker, Reviewer, Curator and Consolidator seats are sent back; the Manager, the Orchestrator, the Architect and every other role keep MIK-R172's line.

The line carries the ended turn's last non-empty line of the agent's own text, shortened to 300 characters; a turn with no such text says `no text` and an unreadable timeline says `unreadable`, and the line still goes out.

The recorded parent receives the line while its record exists and it is not archived, including when its session is closed; otherwise the current Manager of the agent's master does, and a line already held is re-resolved at send time.

Each current-generation decision row goes to turn-ends.jsonl, turned over at 2 MiB with one archive and one error report. The separate declared-wait signal can update host-activity.json by publishing the declaration and next check, removing checkDueAt when the check is spent and clearing declaredWait at wait end. It preserves host-owned state and eventAt.
The plugin's cleanup clears pending and in-flight waits, the per-seat runs and the open declarations, so a reload begins afresh.

A seat whose publication shows a running subagent is left alone at its end and gets nothing at the end of the wait, and the end is not counted; for an open seat, when the last running subagent finishes outside a turn the plugin starts the 60 s wait for that left-alone end once and judges archive, permission, turn and subagent again.

A seat the limit file names as limited gets no seat message and no marked line; the plugin arms one resume at the reset plus 60 seconds, re-arms it when the reset moves later, and cancels it when the seat's own turn starts.

A limited parent retains its owed line until it can receive it. A held recipient's eligible messages resume after the limit clears, subject to archive or absence confirmation and the bounded drain cursor.

The limit is read from the file the serving side wrote and from nothing else: a missing file, an unreadable one, or a report without a limit means no limit, and neither a subagent-holding end nor a limited one counts toward the count of 2.

A seat declares a helper wait when its own last assistant message holds a line that starts `WAITING FOR SUBAGENTS:` after leading spaces, Markdown markers or quoting marks, on any line of that message; the comparison is case-sensitive, only the turn's last assistant message is read, a seat on any provider can declare, and no helper call is ever read as a declaration; a line that starts `WAITING FOR BACKGROUND:` is read the same way as a background declaration.

A declaration alone never increments the silent-end run or gives the parent a line. A real handoff follows ordinary parent-line rules, including suppression by a delivered return, and it resets the run as usual. A non-plug-in opening message also resets the run.

An eligible declaring end opens or renews a wait and records that declaration's ordinal. One check can arm for the current generation and declaration after any handoff path returns, if a slot is available. The check uses the helper delay of three minutes or the background delay, using the earlier time when both are declared; the check names the seat's role, agent and task and asks for each helper with what it does, its status and what came back, and asks the seat to declare again or go on; it takes the seat message's gates — never into a running turn, the limit resume built from its own text, a permission wait or an unreadable host state re-arming it after the check’s configured delay — and a check not delivered writes its skip with the reason.

The provider verdict is the plugin's own `acp-providers.json`: the Paseo version, the files read, each provider's class, ACP verdict and reason, and the drop-outs kept across restarts, written by staging and rename; a provider that reported a helper call is not ACP for that process or a later one, an unreadable or foreign document leaves every provider out of ACP rather than guessed, and one row per provider per process names an unread verdict.

The launch appends the declaration instruction to a seat the verdict puts on ACP before the hand-over artifact is published, so the stored first message and a retry's byte check range over one text, and the receipt records the verdict it acted on with the reason it added or skipped the sentence.

An inactive seat cannot arm a new check. The ordinary close hook ends the wait with its close reason. Where a capped pending wait sheds its own check, the skip row is the only row that undelivered check produces. Ordinary wakes keep their ordinary send-skipped row.
A close stops the seat's own waits, self-wake and limit resume. It preserves lines held to or about the seat. An active turn-end continuation may finish its parent notification after the close.
exclusions: The host and its SDK, Hermes and its ACP adapter, `delegate_task` and `/goal` are outside this obligation.

The product's held-message store, `host-activity.json`'s schema and every Python part of the product are not read for this rule, save the launch that appends the instruction and the reader of the plugin's verdict file.
The role and operation texts of the lifecycle skill carry no part of it; the message carries its own sentences.
No live-host delivery, plugin load or semantic acceptance is claimed; the suite is a host-free composition, and the log is the plugin's own record of decisions, not a census of host deliveries.
The held-message sweep's own delivery is INV-4DQMNE's clause, not this one; this record owns which end is acted on and which line is sent.
The presenter's send holds no role seat and is out of scope.

The host's provider registry, its agent clients and the ACP protocol are read as data; no behaviour of them is claimed, and a published verdict is that plugin's own decision, not a proof about another machine.
A turn ending with an `IDENTITY MISMATCH:` line is not a silent end; it skips the 60-second wait and seat wakes and delivers the mismatch line straight to the parent under BUG-R51@v1 §4.

evidence: 17 host-free node decision tests incl. sealed overlap/restart schedules (L117-C1-F06); publish/round-trip tests; checks-attempt4/plugin-turn-ended.log; worker report Attempt 4

statement: A silent role-agent turn end — a completed turn that hands off to no one, does not end with an `IDENTITY MISMATCH:` line, declares no helper or background wait, that nothing holds and that is not a reply to a waiting sender — wakes the agent that waits, its recorded parent or the current Manager of its master when that parent is archived or missing, with one line naming the role, agent, task, the ended turn's own last line of text and the newest report, except that a Worker, Reviewer, Curator or Consolidator is sent back to its work at the first two silent ends in a row and only from the third gives its parent that line, marked with the count; a delivered return to the parent in that turn suppresses the line wherever the row shows the recipient, a turn with no text says so, and a recipient that is in a turn is told when that turn ends rather than steered into it, unless the product knows that provider keeps its turn under a steer. A seat whose publication shows a running subagent is not a silent end and is left alone at that end, and a provider limit delays the send-back: a seat the limit file names as limited gets neither the seat message nor the counted line until its reset. A limited parent's line is held and flushed once that parent is no longer limited. A provider-limited recipient’s held messages stay queued unless confirmed archive or absence resolves them undelivered. After reset, eligible messages drain when the bounded receipt cursor reaches the recipient. A role seat on any provider may declare a helper or background-process wait. A declaration alone sends no parent line. A handoff in the same turn retains the ordinary recipient and suppression rules. A current declaration can arm one check after that path returns. A later undeclared end, close or archive ends the wait. The plug-in provider verdict still determines the ACP launch instruction and the wake message's closing sentence.
title: Silent role-agent turn-end notification and wake policy
